evidence_ref: requests GHSA-9hjg-9r4m-mvj7 upstream trigger evidence chain
evidence_note: Trigger semantics are derived from OSV/GitHub Advisory, Requests 2.32.3 source, the upstream fix PR and commit, and public exploit discussion. The selected static rule recognizes a literal HTTP(S) URL whose authority user-info causes the legacy netloc-derived .netrc lookup host to differ from the actual parsed hostname. A structural URL match does not prove that .netrc credentials exist, that trust_env remains enabled, or that a malicious redirect target is statically observable.

scope.note: The <2.32.4 range is the vulnerability scope. The selected requests.get API form is a controlled representative call shape and does not redefine the full vulnerability entrypoint set. API History and S_api will be resolved separately. The current static Trigger rule captures the crafted URL authority structure, while .netrc availability, trust_env state, and runtime redirects remain environment/runtime evidence.

fix_evidence.mechanism: Use the parsed URL hostname for .netrc credential lookup instead of deriving the lookup host by splitting netloc.

sources.claim: OSV records Requests versions prior to 2.32.4 as affected and identifies 2.32.4 as the fixed release.
The advisory states that maliciously crafted URLs may cause .netrc credentials to leak in Requests releases before 2.32.4 and identifies trust_env=False as a workaround.
Requests 2.32.3 derives the .netrc lookup host from urlparse(url).netloc by splitting on a colon.

sources.locator: Only use hostname to do netrc lookup instead of netloc
sources.claim: The upstream pull request applies the security fix for GHSA-9hjg-9r4m-mvj7.
The fix replaces the legacy netloc splitting logic with ri.hostname for .netrc lookup.
Public security discussion demonstrates that a redirect may lead Requests to a crafted URL such as http://github.com:@evil.example.net, illustrating the user-info hostname-confusion structure.
